purpose: Every corpus case where `node bin/smithers.js check` disagrees with the case's declared expectation. The conformance runner measures two BACKENDS; neither is the shipped CLI, so this file is the written record of how far the product is from the contract the corpus is quoted as stating. `direction` product-accepts is the dangerous one — the corpus requires a refusal and the product compiled it. `verdict` says which side is wrong; `decision-needed` rows may not be moved by either side until the decisions ledger owner settles them. A row disappears when the divergence is FIXED, never when it is tolerated. The `total` field records the corpus size at the last revision and is DESCRIPTIVE, not a gate: it has gone stale twice (424 -> 438 -> 465) simply because the corpus grows, and gating on its equality would train re-baselining rather than catch anything. The gate is the divergence SET.

divergences.note: src/cli.ts:753-777 runs buildRelativeRuntimeGraph before the semantic stage and returns as soon as it has anything to say. Here it does not even produce a diagnostic: it throws a TypeError that backendFailure (src/cli.ts:1418-1432) turns into a code-less, position-less SMITHERS_PROJECT_ERROR, so the rule the corpus pins is never reached. ADDED 2026-08-27, and its ABSENCE was the interesting part. This case was not listed before, which read as agreement between the product and the corpus. The conformance JS backend runs compileDurableSource itself before compiling (conformance/runner/js-lower.mjs:62-127, :286-337): it locates the durable(...) call site, replaces it with the static Plan descriptor and erases the smithers:flows import. src/cli.ts has no durable stage in check or run — compileDurableSource is reached only from `smithers plan --bindings` (src/cli.ts:1940-1959), which lowers ONE file, requires a bindings file, and neither checks nor runs the program. So the import of smithers:flows survives into the emitted TypeScript and the stock checker answers TS2307/TS2339/TS7006, or — where the Action call is written with the propagation operator — the semantic stage answers SMITHERS1207 because Action.run is not typed as a Result without the lowering. NOT 'the durable feature does not exist': `smithers plan --bindings` works and test/durable.test.mjs exercises the library API directly. The accurate statement is narrower and still serious: check and run perform no durable source lowering, so all 20 green 17-durable rows on the scoreboard rest on harness-only plumbing.
